ports.note: A transform, not a source. Takes CRS84 points and returns the same records projected into the declared UTM zone, in metres. The output is a PROJECTED points value: its spatialReference carries units 'metre' and axis order 'easting-northing', and executionPlan refuses to connect it to any widget that assumes degrees.

ontology.note: No coordinate-transformation activity class or runtime SHACL shape is defined, so this step writes no typed RDF of its own and the status is a gap rather than a partial alignment. What the projection does reach RDF through is the consuming view: a Table output renders the geometry with the OGC IRI of the frame the coordinates are actually in, rather than the fixed CRS84 it asserted before 2026-10-13.

implementation.note: src/reproject-ui.ts was deleted with this release: the file dialog belonged to the acquiring contract, and the sources read UTM themselves from 0.2.0 of the import path.

changes.description: Split: the widget stopped importing its own data and became a points-to-points transform, projecting CRS84 into a UTM zone.
changes.migration: A node saved under 0.1.0 carries params.data holding points the old widget had ALREADY converted to CRS84 at import. validateWorkflow rewrites such a node to point_input with those records, its label and its connections kept, and stamps sourceMigration.fromType 'reproject'. Recorded as a RecontractedNodeType: the type was neither retired nor renamed, its contract changed.
changes.direction: CRS84 -> UTM, which is the only direction that composes. After the source CRS rule every source emits CRS84, so nothing upstream produces projected points for an inverse transform to consume.

changes.description: Import-time projection change from WGS84 UTM metres to CRS84 degrees; see docs/experiments/40-reprojection-primitives.md. WGS84 zones only, no datum shift, no raster warping. Narrower than the general Reproject node proposed in experiment 05.

evidence.note: Unit checks assert UTM definitional invariants (false easting and northing, symmetry about the central meridian), round-trip error within 0.01 m and guard refusals. Independently compared against pyproj 3.8.0 / PROJ 9.8.1 over nine points in zone 35 south: maximum separation 6.70e-05 m against a 1 mm tolerance, explained by the nine-decimal coordinate rounding (see docs/experiments/41-validation-lab.md). That comparison ran in CPython, not a browser kernel, covers one zone, and establishes no datum other than WGS84.
